test_title: PYST 3: SSC JE EE- General Awareness (Held on: 16 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements about the retreating monsoon of India.

1) The months of October and November are known for retreating monsoons.

2) The South-west monsoons becomes South-east monsoons.

3) A bulk of the rainfall of the Coromondal coast is derived from these depressions and cyclones.

4) In northern India, it is comparatively dry and temperatures begin to fall.

5) Three-fourths of the total rain in the country is received during the retreating monsoon season.

Which of the above are true?
solution:
The correct answer is **Only statements 1, 3, and 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the months of **October-November**, the **southwest monsoon** winds become** weaker** and start to **retreat** to the **northeast region** i.e. from the **skies of North India**. this phase of the monsoon is called as **Retreating monsoon season.**
 
• During this season as the **Coromondal cost** is closer to the **sea region a bulk of rainfall is derived **due to the **cyclone and depressions** produced in the seas.
 
• In northern India, it is **comparatively dry and temperatures** begin to** fall. **In **southern India**, it is **cool and heavy rainfall begins** near the regions of Coromondal cost.
 
• Rather than these facts, only **10% of the total rain **in the country is received during the retreating monsoon season.
 
• This shows that **only statements 1, 3, and 4 are true **but others are false.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• With the onsets of retreating monsoons, **skies become clearer and clouds disappear**.
 
• The **pressure gradient **becomes **low**.
 
• **Tamil Nadu** receives **half of the rainfall** during this time, this season is also called as **North-East Monsoon season**.
